children: Rahul Murarka will leave after more than five years as CFO, giving Vedant Fashions nearly two months to manage the finance leadership transition

Vedant Fashions Chief Financial Officer (CFO) Rahul Murarka will step down from his role effective 14 November 2026 to pursue new professional opportunities. Murarka has served as CFO since 17 May 2021, and his departure comes after more than five years with the company, creating a defined transition period for succession planning and handover.
Murarka has led the company’s finance function since May 2021. His exit will bring to an end a tenure of more than five years at Vedant Fashions.

The company has not named a successor so far. With the resignation becoming effective on 14 November, Vedant Fashions has close to two months to manage the transition and identify a new finance chief.

The leadership change comes as Vedant Fashions continues to report growth in its financial performance. Standalone net profit for Q1 FY27 rose 14.73 per cent year-on-year to Rs 80.61 crore, while revenue from operations increased 7.17 per cent to Rs 301.37 crore.

The company also reported a gross margin of 65.7 per cent during the quarter. The numbers provide the financial backdrop against which the CFO transition will take place and will remain relevant as the next finance leader takes charge.

Murarka’s resignation follows other board-level changes at Vedant Fashions in recent months. Nihir Parikh and Neetu Kashiramka were appointed as Additional Independent Directors on 2 September, while Tarun Puri completed his term as an Independent Director on 5 September.
In July, the company also extended the tenures of members of its senior leadership for another five years, adding further context to the ongoing changes at the top.

The immediate focus will now shift to succession and continuity within the finance function. The incoming CFO will be responsible for maintaining financial reporting, planning, governance and capital discipline while ensuring a smooth handover from Murarka.

The transition period before Murarka’s departure gives Vedant Fashions time to complete the succession process without an abrupt leadership gap. The appointment of a replacement will determine how the company structures its finance leadership after 14 November and will form part of its wider management transition.
